drugRefs.why: Provides reliable coverage of oral anaerobes alongside typical community pathogens, addressing the polymicrobial nature of aspiration pneumonia in a single well-tolerated agent.

drugRefs.coverage: Strong anaerobic coverage; reasonable alternative in penicillin allergy, though lacks reliable gram-negative coverage.
Broader coverage including anaerobes and gram-negatives for hospital-associated aspiration or more severe presentations.

coverageMatrix.completeness: Amoxicillin-clavulanate covers the core polymicrobial flora for community-acquired aspiration.
gaps: MRSA not reliably covered by any of these - add vancomycin/linezolid only with specific risk factors.

stewardship.deescalation: Narrow or stop anaerobic-specific coverage if cultures (when obtained) do not support it and the patient is improving on a narrower-spectrum agent; reassess for evolving lung abscess if response is slow.

drugs.why: Provides reliable coverage of oral anaerobes alongside typical community pathogens, addressing the polymicrobial nature of aspiration pneumonia in a single well-tolerated agent.

drugs.coverage: Strong anaerobic coverage; reasonable alternative in penicillin allergy, though lacks reliable gram-negative coverage.
Broader coverage including anaerobes and gram-negatives for hospital-associated aspiration or more severe presentations.

framework: Routine anaerobic coverage is appropriate for witnessed/strongly suspected aspiration - but not for typical CAP without an aspiration history, where it adds unnecessary spectrum.
Address the underlying aspiration risk (dysphagia evaluation, positioning, oral hygiene) as part of management, not antibiotics alone - recurrence is otherwise likely.

De-escalate based on clinical response; prolonged anaerobic coverage beyond 7 days is not routinely needed for uncomplicated aspiration pneumonia (distinct from lung abscess, which needs longer therapy).
